text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager alert — SLO breach detected on /generate-stream (prod). p95=720ms, p99=3.2s, streaming stall rate ~6% over last 5m. Root signal: high preproc latency. Paging oncall: jess

jess: I'm on it. pulling traces + top logs now. @csm-ana any customer reports?

csm-ana: AcmeHealth reported degraded streaming at ~10:12 UTC. No dropped data but UI stalls and long waits. They run high-volume JSON-mode jobs. I've opened a high-touch channel with them.

matt: Traces look like preproc-service doing heavy prompt/template expansion for JSON mode + tool-schema validation. Recent renderer change (deploy 3123) appears correlated — some requests balloon token counts. p99 preproc_time_ms ~= 2500 in traces.

sasha: Confirmed: deploy/3123 to preproc-service at 10:08 rolled a new template renderer. We see nested tool-schema expansion paths causing combinatorial template interpolation for some customer schemas. Logs:

```
2026-03-15T10:12:05Z preproc INFO request_id=abc123 preproc_time_ms=2523 template_tokens=4892 mode=json tool_schema_size=12
2026-03-15T10:12:06Z preproc WARN request_id=abc124 preproc_time_ms=1980 template_tokens=3401 mode=json
```

lee: Can we flip the feature flag to disable full tool-schema expansion in JSON mode and fall back to the legacy renderer? That should massively reduce tokens for affected requests.

priya: I can flip the flag. Flag endpoint: `feature.flags.json_full_expand`. Plan: set false, then restart preproc pods to pick up config. Rolling now.

priya: Executing:
```
curl -XPOST "https://config.internal/flags/json_full_expand" -d '{"value":false}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
kubectl rollout restart deploy/preproc-service -n prod
```

oncall-bot: Feature flag set to false by priya — restart triggered. Expect new renderer within ~45s. Continuing to monitor p95/p99 and streaming stall metric.

matt: After flag flip, p99 down to ~1.1s and p95 ~430ms within 3m. Streaming stalls down to ~0.9%. Looks like mitigation working.

jess: Good catch. Need a durable fix: limit template expansion depth, add per-request token guard, and cache tokenized templates keyed by tool-schema hash. Also tighten validation so schema growth doesn't blow up tokens.

sasha: I've opened PR #482 to add expansion depth limit + early bail when estimated token_count > 2000 and to add a cache layer (LRU by schema hash). Link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/preproc/pulls/482

priya: I'll run hotfix through staging smoke tests — ETA ~30m to prod if green. Quick notes: will also add a metric for 'template_expansion_tokens' to alert earlier.

csm-ana: Communicated mitigation to AcmeHealth and that we disabled the new expansion behavior temporarily. They're relieved and asked for an RCA + ETA for a permanent fix.

ops-bot: Created incident page: https://status.redwood.internal/incidents/3123456789 — added customer impact: AcmeHealth streaming degradation, partial UX stalls, no data loss. Severity classified as Sev2.

jess: I'll own the postmortem. Initial timeline + actions to include: 1) rollback dangerous expansion by flag (done), 2) hotfix PR for bounds+cache (in review), 3) add pre-deploy schema regression test, 4) alert for high template_tokens, 5) customer follow-up and remediation note.

matt: Also note: tokenizer cost spike — when template tokens balloon, downstream tokenizer CPU spikes and KV cache misses amplify tail. We'll add a short-term mitigator to cap template tokenization concurrency per pod.

lee: Agreed. I'll add a conservative concurrency limiter in the preproc k8s HPA and implement a per-pod tokenization semaphore in the hotfix.

jess: Thanks team. Next: confirm post-fix metrics remain stable for 2h, then schedule RCA write-up and notify customers. Marking incident as 'mitigated' once p99 stable < 1.5s for 30m.

priya: Deploying hotfix to prod in 22m after staging smoke. Will update thread.

ops-bot: Note for handoff: oncall until 12:00 UTC — if template tokens re-spike, page oncall.

jess: Closing loop — mitigation in place, customer notified, hotfix queued. I'll postmortem and link to PR + logs. Good work. :thumbsup:
